fit.gap_handling_summary: The application demonstrates a strong real match on the core stack, measurable mobile performance, accessibility remediation, integrations and regulated fintech delivery. It correctly retains WCAG 2.1 AA rather than claiming the employer's 2.2 AA standard, and does not invent healthcare, GDPR or OWASP expertise. Health-data learning readiness and explicit semantic/responsive implementation remain unaddressed; German proficiency is slightly polished beyond the source qualification.

issues: The extensive skills inventory and repeated per-employer technology lists dilute the otherwise well-targeted achievements.
School education, driving licence and references add little for an experienced full-stack application.
Testing is largely a tool inventory in the CV; the letter more clearly states unit and end-to-end testing.
German should retain a qualification reflecting that most school knowledge has been forgotten.
The GitHub handle and blog are supplied, but a direct URL to a relevant built project would be more useful to the employer.

reasons: The single-column PDF extracts in the correct order with intact words, contact details and recognizable section headings.
All principal stack requirements are explicit, with current React/TypeScript work dating from 2021.
Git workflow experience is evidenced through GitHub Actions and GitLab CI rather than a standalone Git keyword.
WCAG 2.1 AA is relevant evidence but not an exact match for WCAG 2.2 AA.
Security/privacy keywords and explicit test categories are weaker in the CV; missing expertise must not be inserted simply to improve matching.

issues: Testing is repeated in consecutive sentences: “write automated tests with Jest and Playwright” followed by “use Jest for unit testing and Playwright for end-to-end testing.”
The technical inventory in the third paragraph is dense and could be shortened in favour of a clearer connection to patient booking or intake workflows.
The letter does not explicitly address learning the health-data privacy requirements; it appropriately avoids asserting existing GDPR expertise.
The company-specific content is accurate but mainly references the advertised principles rather than the company's particular products or recent patient-app work.
strengths: Correctly names Verdane Care, the Full-Stack Engineer role and the Patient Experience team.
Uses concrete, supported conversion and mobile-performance outcomes.
Connects sensitive fintech flows to privacy-conscious patient-facing work without claiming healthcare experience.
Accurately distinguishes the candidate's WCAG 2.1 AA work from the employer's target standard.
Confirms fluent professional English and includes no unsupported work-arrangement commitment.

spacing_issues: The CV's first page is dense, while the second page is only 44.7% filled, leaving a large lower blank area.
The Nordkust role is split so its standalone “Technologies” line begins page two without the employer heading or responsibilities.
issues: The 10-point CV body is readable but compact; reducing repeated technology inventories would allow a more comfortable layout.
The letter is clean and comfortably readable at 11 points. Its lower-page whitespace is normal for a short letter.

fluency_and_tone_issues: “English is my fluent work language at Älvgrind” is awkward; “I am fluent in English, my working language at Älvgrind” is more natural.
The CV summary switches from the implied subject in “Specialised in” to “Has delivered”; this is understandable but stylistically uneven.
“write automated tests with Jest and Playwright” and “use Jest for unit testing and Playwright for end-to-end testing” repeat the same point in the letter.

parsed.summary: Both documents present a strong, largely faithful match through the candidate's React/TypeScript, NestJS, PostgreSQL, accessibility and measurable performance experience. The letter is correctly targeted and makes a credible connection between sensitive fintech workflows and patient-facing software without inventing healthcare or GDPR expertise. The main accuracy concern is the omission of the qualification that the candidate's school German is mostly forgotten. The PDFs are readable and ATS-friendly, but repeated technology lists, a stranded continuation line on CV page two and repetitive testing language reduce polish. Work-arrangement preferences are correctly left open; the job offers Graz hybrid working or remote work within the four specified countries.
